name: Mel
notes: Opens by auto-attacking (applying the first Overwhelm stack), then fires Radiant Volley (Q) and Solar Snare (E) as soon as each comes off cooldown, weaving attacks between casts; Golden Eclipse (R) is held until Q and E have each landed once so it detonates against a meaningfully stacked target, then fired as soon as legal and never again (its cooldown far exceeds the fight length).
Rebuttal (W) is never cast: see "unused".W below.

Radiant Volley's 0.5s bolt channel and Solar Snare's orb travel time are treated as landing instantly on cast (only the usual 0.25s cast-time lockout applies), matching how a single stationary hitbox receives every bolt/orb regardless of travel; each of Q's several explosions and each of E's field ticks is still dealt as its own damage instance, each applying its own Overwhelm stack.

Solar Snare's field is modeled as 4 ticks (its 0.5s DoT duration over the 0.125s tick interval from the numbers sheet), starting immediately on the orb's impact; the 0.5s expansion delay only affects radius, not tick timing, and is not modeled.

Overwhelm's stored-damage figures (flat + per-stack) are read from the numbers-sheet bin (MelR.BasePassiveFlatDamage/BasePassiveStackDamage, ranks 1-3) plus the wiki's rank-0 values (50 flat / 2 per stack, active even before Golden Eclipse is ranked); these two sources agree once combined (e.g. 50+10=60), resolving the dossier's flagged discrepancy rather than leaving it open.

Overwhelm's burst-release condition ('stored post-mitigation damage exceeds the target's current health') is approximated by comparing the raw (pre-mitigation) stored magic damage against the dummy's current health, since the driver has no access to the engine's internal mitigation math; this can only ever add extra true-to-source magic damage, never remove any.

Searing Brilliance's bonus blazing projectiles from an empowered attack are each treated as their own Overwhelm-stacking damage instance (one interpretation of an unsettled dossier question), since they are direct hits from Mel rather than an itemized on-hit effect.
Mana costs are not modeled: nothing here binds inside a 15s fight at level 16.

unused.W: Rebuttal's only offensive effect is reflecting an enemy champion's projectile back at them as magic damage; a stationary target dummy never casts anything or fires a projectile at Mel, so W can never trigger its damage component in this fight. Its shield and move speed are pure survival/positioning and irrelevant to a damage race. Casting it would only spend mana (unmodeled) for zero damage, so the driver never casts it.
